info.title: localpost shared daemon API
info.description:
Canonical contract for the implemented shared loopback daemon. The info version identifies the 0.2.0 release-candidate API description; it is independent of the OpenAPI specification version. This document does not assert that the release has been published.

All three routes share one plain HTTP listener bound to IPv4 loopback 127.0.0.1. There is no authentication, authorization token, credential requirement, origin registration, or origin allowlist. Registration IDs address mailboxes and are not secrets. Startup requires --mailbox-root identifying an existing absolute writable directory. The daemon canonicalizes and probes the root before listening. Registration creates a private UUIDv4-named child and returns its absolute canonical path. POSIX mailboxes use 0700 permissions and delivery files use 0600. Windows mailboxes and files inherit the operator-provisioned root ACL. Registrations live only in memory and disappear on process exit; delivery files remain.

CORS: every application response, including application errors, sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, and Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, DELETE, OPTIONS. The supported API prefix is /api/2026-11-05. Unsupported /api/ prefixes and retired /registrations routes return 404 unsupported_api_version with a message naming the supported prefix, including OPTIONS. Supported-prefix OPTIONS requests return 204 before route/ID validation and create no file or registration. Unrelated unknown paths return 404 not_found, including OPTIONS. No Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is sent. Browser callers should omit credentials; application CSP and browser local-network permissions still apply.

Routing is case-sensitive except for hexadecimal letters in UUIDv4 path IDs, which are normalized to lowercase. Unknown paths, including the obsolete bare /messages route, return 404 with not_found. Under the supported prefix, trailing slashes are not normalized: /registrations/ is treated as a malformed ID (400), while /registrations/{id}/ and /registrations/{id}/messages/ are unrecognized paths (404). Malformed UUIDv4 route IDs return 400 with invalid_registration_id; well-formed unknown or retired IDs return 404 with registration_not_found. On recognized routes, unsupported methods return 405 with Allow: POST or DELETE, subject to the route/ID/admission checks described by each operation. OPTIONS bypasses those checks.

Responses below describe application-handler JSON envelopes. Malformed HTTP headers, invalid framing rejected before handler dispatch, and other net/http transport rejections may instead produce a transport-level response or close the connection, without this JSON envelope or application CORS headers. The server allows 5 seconds for request headers and 30 seconds for control-request reading; uploads override the body deadline with a 30-second progress-based idle deadline. Rejected or incomplete bodies may cause connection closure; successful body consumption allows normal keep-alive reuse.

Fixed limits: 64 live registrations and 16 admitted uploads globally. Closing registrations retain capacity through cleanup, and upload slots remain held through publication and the temporary-file cleanup attempt. The 160 MiB aggregate maximum of admitted payload bytes does not bound all memory, retained files, or failed-cleanup leftovers. Shutdown stops new work and provides one shared 30-second grace deadline before interruption; filesystem cleanup can take longer. There is no durable queue, automatic retry, or power-loss durability guarantee.

servers.description: One shared IPv4 loopback listener. The operator may select an unprivileged port with --port (1024-65535); occupied ports fail startup rather than silently changing.

port.description: Operator-selected listener port; default 53147, accepted range 1024-65535. Not a per-registration port.

post.summary: Allocate and register a private mailbox
post.description:
Accepts exactly one empty JSON object {} and creates a new UUIDv4-named directory under the configured canonical mailbox root before exposing the registration. Returns exactly id and directory. Existing paths are never adopted or overwritten. UUID collisions are retried a bounded number of times. Allocation failures leave no active registration or consumed capacity. Registrations disappear on restart, while directories and files remain. A lost response can leave an orphaned mailbox, and retries can create additional mailboxes. Agents manage retention and retire registrations before removing their own files and directory.

Media-type parameters such as charset=utf-8 are accepted. The control body limit is 65,536 bytes including whitespace, with a 30-second read budget. At most 64 registrations may be live; closing registrations retain capacity through cleanup. Saturation rejects immediately.

requestBody.description: Exactly one empty JSON object {}. Empty bodies, null, arrays, multiple objects and every field, including the former directory field in any case, are rejected. Content-Type application/json is mandatory; x-required-request-headers records this because OpenAPI ignores Content-Type Header Parameters.

200.description: Private mailbox directory created and registered. Exactly id and directory are returned; the directory basename equals the lowercase UUIDv4 id.

400.description: Malformed, missing, non-object, trailing or nonempty JSON, or an unreadable or timed-out control body. Stable error code invalid_request.

405.description: A non-POST method on this path, except OPTIONS. Stable error code: `method_not_allowed`.

413.description: Registration body exceeds 65,536 bytes, for known-length or streamed requests. Stable error code: `request_too_large`.

415.description: Missing, malformed, or unsupported Content-Type; application/json is required. Stable error code: `unsupported_media_type`.

503.description: Registration allocation is stopping/unavailable, or all 64 registration slots are owned. Stable error codes: `unavailable`, `registration_limit`.

500.description: Mailbox allocation failed because filesystem creation failed or bounded UUID collision retries were exhausted. No registration or capacity is retained. Stable error code mailbox_allocation_failed.

options.description: Returns before route, ID, method, media-type or body validation for the supported API prefix. No registration or file is created. Unsupported /api/ prefixes and retired unversioned /registrations routes instead return 404 unsupported_api_version with the supported prefix in the error message. Unrelated unknown paths return 404 not_found, including OPTIONS.

delete.summary: Retire one mailbox and finish its cleanup
delete.description:
Stops new uploads for this mailbox, then allows already accepted requests a 30-second grace period. Remaining requests are interrupted at the deadline; progress does not extend it. The response waits for request cleanup attempts, including filesystem operations that can outlast the deadline. It does not shut down the shared listener or affect sibling mailboxes. Completed delivery files remain untouched.

Concurrent DELETE requests while the mailbox is closing join the same operation. Once removal finishes, another DELETE returns 404. Disconnecting the DELETE client does not cancel cleanup; a lost response leaves its outcome uncertain. No request body or Content-Type is required; a supplied body is not used. Whole-daemon shutdown uses one shared grace deadline rather than 30 seconds per mailbox.

The mailbox directory and delivered files remain after retirement. The agent may remove its own mailbox only after retirement completes. Restart also retains directories but invalidates registrations.

200.description: Mailbox removed after accepted request cleanup attempts finish. The returned ID is lowercase even when the path ID used uppercase.

400.description: ID does not have canonical UUIDv4 structure and RFC variant (hex letter case is accepted). Stable error code: `invalid_registration_id`.

404.description: Well-formed registration ID is unknown or already retired. Stable error code: `registration_not_found`.

405.description: A non-DELETE method on this path, except OPTIONS. ID validation happens first. Stable error code: `method_not_allowed`.

options.description: Returns before route, ID, method, media-type or body validation for the supported API prefix. No registration or file is created. Unsupported /api/ prefixes and retired unversioned /registrations routes instead return 404 unsupported_api_version with the supported prefix in the error message. Unrelated unknown paths return 404 not_found, including OPTIONS.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Path segment for this documented route. OPTIONS does not validate UUID syntax or registration existence; arbitrary segments are accepted.

post.summary: Deliver one opaque body as one complete file
post.description:
Accepts application/octet-stream or application/json, with valid media-type parameters. BOTH media types carry opaque bytes: JSON-labelled input can contain invalid JSON, arbitrary binary bytes, or no bytes. There is no JSON parsing, schema validation, string wrapping, base64 encoding, decoding, newline insertion, or content decompression. HTTP transfer framing is removed; content-encoded body bytes are stored as received.

The body limit is 10,485,760 bytes (10 MiB), inclusive; zero-byte files are valid. The upload read deadline resets on progress, allowing uploads longer than 30 seconds, but 30 seconds of stalled reading causes a timeout. This is distinct from the control-request read budget and the teardown grace period, and does not impose a deadline on OS filesystem calls.

At most 16 uploads are admitted across all mailboxes; a slot is held through publication and the temporary-file cleanup attempt. Saturation rejects immediately without a queue or retry. Closing mailboxes reject new requests with 503 until removed, then return 404.

A temporary file is written and closed before a same-directory hard link publishes the complete final file without overwriting an existing destination. Hard-link support is required; failure does not fall back to partial-file visibility. Temporary-name removal is best effort, and its failure after successful publication does not change success. Consumers must read only final localpost_[UUIDv7].dat names and manage retention.

A 200 response means publication completed, not durable persistence across power loss. No ordering across concurrent requests, durable queue, replay, recovery, or automatic retry is provided. A lost response can leave a published file; retrying can duplicate a message. Include any desired sequence/deduplication information in your own opaque payload.

requestBody.description: Raw HTTP body, including an empty body. An accepted Content-Type is still required for empty uploads. These media entries deliberately omit schemas so no JSON data model or base64/string representation is imposed. For example, the raw ASCII bytes `{not JSON` are accepted with either media type, and an empty byte sequence is accepted with either media type. The application/json label never causes validation or repair. Content-Type is mandatory even when the body is empty; x-required-request-headers records this constraint because OpenAPI ignores Content-Type Header Parameters.

200.description: Complete file published; receipt byte count includes exactly the preserved body bytes. Temporary cleanup is best effort.

400.description: Invalid UUIDv4 path ID, or the handler cannot read a complete HTTP body. Invalid JSON payload content is not an error. Stable error codes: `invalid_registration_id`, `invalid_request`.

404.description: Well-formed registration ID is unknown or retired. Route mismatches elsewhere return not_found as described in the API overview. Stable error code: `registration_not_found`.

405.description: A non-POST method on a live mailbox route, except OPTIONS. ID existence and mailbox admission are checked first. Stable error code: `method_not_allowed`.

408.description: An upload body read timed out, including stalled reads; a forced teardown can interrupt a read as well. Stable error code: `request_timeout`.

413.description: Body exceeds 10,485,760 bytes, for known-length or streamed requests. Stable error code: `request_too_large`.

415.description: Missing, malformed, or unsupported Content-Type. The two documented media types are accepted, with parameters. Stable error code: `unsupported_media_type`.

500.description: Temporary-file creation, write, close, or publication failed; read-deadline enforcement or interrupted completion can also fail. No success receipt is issued. Stable error code: `delivery_failed`.

503.description: Mailbox is closing, or all 16 global upload slots are owned. Stable error codes: `unavailable`, `upload_limit`.

options.description: Returns before route, ID, method, media-type or body validation for the supported API prefix. No registration or file is created. Unsupported /api/ prefixes and retired unversioned /registrations routes instead return 404 unsupported_api_version with the supported prefix in the error message. Unrelated unknown paths return 404 not_found, including OPTIONS.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Path segment for this documented route. OPTIONS does not validate UUID syntax or registration existence; arbitrary segments are accepted.

RegistrationId.description: Canonical lowercase RFC-variant UUIDv4 registration identity. This is a mailbox address, not an authentication credential. It is unrelated to the UUIDv7 used in delivery filenames.

RegistrationRequest.description: Exactly one empty JSON object. No fields or former directory aliases are accepted.

Registration.description: Exactly id and directory. The absolute canonical directory is a newly created direct child of the configured root and its basename equals id. This cross-field equality is verified by clients; JSON Schema does not express it.

forced.description: True when the grace deadline required interrupting remaining requests. It does not assert that filesystem cleanup finished within 30 seconds.

filename.description: Basename of the complete published file in the registered directory, using an RFC-variant UUIDv7. Never a path or registration ID.

bytes.description: Number of opaque HTTP body bytes written to the file, after HTTP transfer framing is removed.

code.description: Stable application error identifier. Each operation response documents the codes applicable to its status.

message.description: Human-readable detail. Wording is not a stable programmatic contract.

DestinationDirectory.description: Absolute canonical service-side path to the newly allocated mailbox. The basename equals the returned lowercase UUIDv4 id. The parent is the configured canonical mailbox root. Use native host path syntax. The directory remains after DELETE and restart.

RegistrationId.name: id
RegistrationId.description: RFC-variant UUIDv4 in hyphenated form. Hex letters may be uppercase or lowercase; the daemon normalizes to lowercase. Route words remain case-sensitive. This validation applies to control/delivery operations; OPTIONS bypasses it.

Access-Control-Allow-Origin.description: Permissive CORS for application responses; no origin registration.

Access-Control-Allow-Headers.description: The advertised allowed browser request header.

Access-Control-Allow-Methods.description: The shared listener advertises these methods on every application response.

Preflight.description: CORS preflight accepted with no body, registration or file. Applies to supported-version paths regardless of ID validity or existence. Unsupported /api/ prefixes and retired unversioned /registrations routes return 404 unsupported_api_version instead. Unrelated unknown paths return 404 not_found.

x-unsupported-api-version.description: All methods, including OPTIONS, under unsupported /api/ prefixes or retired unversioned /registrations routes return the standard Error envelope. The message names /api/2026-11-05. All three CORS headers retain their documented values.
